sentences.en: As the NFL season comes to a close, a former head coach of the Miami Dolphins has filed a class action lawsuit against the league, accusing it of racial discrimination
sentences.zh: 随着 NFL 赛季接近尾声，迈阿密海豚队的一位前主教练对该联盟提起了一项集体诉讼，指控其存在种族歧视，

sentences.en: in its hiring practices.
sentences.zh: 特别是在招聘行为方面。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Ken Belson, spoke to the civil rights lawyer who created the policy at the center of the lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事肯·贝尔森采访了这位诉讼核心政策的制定者，一位民权律师。

sentences.en: It's Monday, February 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月14日，星期一。

sentences.en: So Ken, catch us up a bit here.
sentences.zh: 那么肯，给我们介绍一下情况吧。

sentences.en: What exactly has been going on with the NFL in this class action lawsuit?
sentences.zh: NFL 这场集体诉讼到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Well, it all starts with a guy named Brian Flores.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这一切都始于一个叫布莱恩·弗洛雷斯的人。

sentences.en: We are delighted now to be joined by Brian Flores, who was the head coach of the Miami
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴现在能请到布莱恩·弗洛雷斯，他曾担任迈阿密

sentences.en: Dolphins for the last several years.
sentences.zh: 海豚队过去几年的主教练。

sentences.en: And who is Brian Flores?
sentences.zh: 那么布莱恩·弗洛雷斯是谁？

sentences.en: Brian Flores is a really interesting character in NFL terMs. He came from Brooklyn, grew up
sentences.zh: 布莱恩·弗洛雷斯在 NFL 圈子里是一个非常有趣的人物。他来自布鲁克林，在那里长大，

sentences.en: there, played football in college, and became a scouting assistant with the New England Patriots during their very successful run of Super Bowl appearances.
sentences.zh: 在大学踢过橄榄球，并在新英格兰爱国者队多次成功打入超级碗期间担任球探助理。

sentences.en: Look, coaching is what I love.
sentences.zh: 听着，执教是我热爱的事业。

sentences.en: It's a passion of mine.
sentences.zh: 这是我的热情所在。

sentences.en: I'm called and gifted to do it.
sentences.zh: 我天生就是干这个的，也有这方面的天赋。

sentences.en: Um, and eventually he got a head coaching job, uh, with the Miami Dolphins in 2019 at a pretty young age.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最终他在2019年以相当年轻的年纪获得了迈阿密海豚队的主教练职位。

sentences.en: And look, the, the National Football League, and I've been in this league 18 years.
sentences.zh: 你看，国家橄榄球联盟，我已经在联盟待了18年了。

sentences.en: He was less than 40 at the time and he had a rocky first season, but the next two seasons he had winning records and almost got the Dolphins into the playoffs, which was a pretty
sentences.zh: 他当时不到40岁，第一个赛季表现平平，但接下来的两个赛季他都取得了胜多负少的战绩，并差点带领海豚队进入季后赛，这对于如此年轻的教练来说，

sentences.en: good track record for such a young coach.
sentences.zh: 是一个相当不错的成绩。

sentences.en: Surprisingly though, he was fired at the end of the season.
sentences.zh: 然而令人惊讶的是，他在赛季结束后被解雇了。

sentences.en: But he did like a lot of coaches, started going on other interviews, uh, for other vacancies.
sentences.zh: 但他像许多教练一样，开始去参加其他职位的面试。

sentences.en: Um, I interviewed for the Giants position.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我参加了巨人队职位的面试。

sentences.en: I was set to...
sentences.zh: 我当时准备……

sentences.en: And one of them was with the New York Giants.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是纽约巨人队。

sentences.en: And three days before his interview, he gets a pretty strange text message.
sentences.zh: 在面试前三天，他收到了一条非常奇怪的短信。

sentences.en: I received the text message, uh, from Bill Belichick saying congratulations on the Giants, essentially a congratulations on the Giants job.
sentences.zh: 我收到了比尔·贝利奇克发来的短信，说祝贺我得到巨人队的工作，基本上就是祝贺我入职。

sentences.en: It's from his former boss and mentor, Bill Belichick.
sentences.zh: 这是来自他以前的老板和导师比尔·贝利奇克。

sentences.en: And Belichick says, um, congratulations, basically.
sentences.zh: 贝利奇克基本上是说，恭喜。

sentences.en: I think you're going to get the job.
sentences.zh: 我想你会得到这份工作的。

sentences.en: And, uh, Brian Flores is sort of confused.
sentences.zh: 然后，布莱恩·弗洛雷斯有点困惑。

sentences.en: I just, uh, I asked him, is this, are you talking to the right Brian?
sentences.zh: 我只是问他，这是……你找对布莱恩了吗？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And I actually asked Belichick, are you talking to me or are you talking to Brian Dable, the guy from Buffalo, that he's texted to the wrong guy named Brian?
sentences.zh: 我实际上问了贝利奇克，你是在跟我说话，还是在跟布法罗的布莱恩·达博尔说话？他是不是发错人了？

sentences.en: And just to clarify, Ken, the other Brian is white?
sentences.zh: 肯，为了澄清一下，另一个布莱恩是白人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the other Brian from the Buffalo Bills is a white candidate.
sentences.zh: 是的，来自布法罗比尔队的另一个布莱恩是一位白人候选人。

sentences.en: And at that point, Bill Belichick realizes what he's done and says, you know, I double checked and misread the text.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，比尔·贝利奇克意识到自己做了什么，并说，你知道，我核对了一下，看错了短信。

sentences.en: I meant to be writing this to Brian Dable.
sentences.zh: 我本想发给布莱恩·达博尔的。

sentences.en: Sorry about that one.
sentences.zh: 抱歉啊。

sentences.en: How did that make you feel, knowing that you were walking into an interview where a decision might have already been made?
sentences.zh: 当你意识到自己去参加面试时，决定可能已经做好了，这让你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: It was a range of emotions, uh, humiliation, uh, disbelief, um, anger.
sentences.zh: 那是一种复杂的情绪，嗯，屈辱，嗯，难以置信，嗯，愤怒。

sentences.en: And that's where Brian Flores, who's black, starts to think that, hmm, this whole process is a sham.
sentences.zh: 这就是身为黑人的布莱恩·弗洛雷斯开始认为，嗯，整个过程是一场骗局的原因。

sentences.en: A few days later, Brian Flores files a federal lawsuit alleging discrimination by the NFL and all of its 32 teams, which is pretty extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 几天后，布莱恩·弗洛雷斯提起了一项联邦诉讼，指控 NFL 及其所有32支球队存在歧视，这非常罕见。

sentences.en: Uh, coaches typically don't go to court to sue their employers, uh, especially when they want to get jobs because it's, um, a very radical move.
sentences.zh: 嗯，教练通常不会去法院起诉他们的雇主，尤其是当他们还想找工作的时候，因为这是一个非常激进的举动。

sentences.en: The crux of it, though, comes down to one rule that the NFL put in place about two decades ago, a rule that actually since then has been widely adopted across corporate America and
sentences.zh: 然而，问题的关键归结为 NFL 大约二十年前制定的一项规则，这项规则实际上自那时起已被美国企业界和

sentences.en: other institutions.
sentences.zh: 其他机构广泛采用。

sentences.en: And that rule is called the Rooney Rule.
sentences.zh: 那项规则被称为“鲁尼规则”。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what is the Rooney Rule?
sentences.zh: 那么什么是鲁尼规则？

sentences.en: Well, the Rooney Rule was created in part by a guy named Cyrus Mary.
sentences.zh: 嗯，鲁尼规则在一定程度上是由一个叫赛勒斯·梅里的人创立的。

sentences.en: Hey, Ken.
sentences.zh: 嘿，肯。

sentences.en: Howdy.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Sorry, I'm late.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我迟到了。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: I have all of the phone calls we've had over the years.
sentences.zh: 我有我们多年来所有的通话记录。

sentences.en: It's the first time I've actually seen you.
sentences.zh: 这是我第一次真正见到你。

sentences.en: So I've known Cyrus for about 10 years now.
sentences.zh: 所以我认识赛勒斯大约10年了。

sentences.en: He's a civil rights lawyer in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 他是华盛顿特区的一名民权律师。

sentences.en: So, um, just to start out, is there a story you can tell us about how you got into civil rights litigation?
sentences.zh: 那么，嗯，先从头说起，你能给我们讲讲你是如何投身民权诉讼的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Um, I'm fortunate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很幸运。

sentences.en: I'm a son of immigrants.
sentences.zh: 我是移民的儿子。

sentences.en: My parents are from Iran.
sentences.zh: 我的父母来自伊朗。

sentences.en: His parents had both moved to America from Iran, and they both had a deep affinity for the civil rights movement in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 他的父母都是从伊朗移民到美国的，他们对20世纪60年代的民权运动有着深厚的共鸣。

sentences.en: I grew up in a household with the Kennedy era idealism infused the household.
sentences.zh: 我在一个充满肯尼迪时代理想主义的家庭中长大。

sentences.en: At the same time, the civil rights movement infused the household.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，民权运动也深深影响了这个家庭。

sentences.en: So as much as my mother believed so much into the ideals of America, she could not overlook the tragedy of race in America.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管我母亲非常相信美国的理想，但她无法忽视美国种族问题的悲剧。

sentences.en: And she essentially, in so many words, expected me to do something to make America a better place.
sentences.zh: 她基本上是用很多话语期望我能做点什么，让美国变得更美好。

sentences.en: So he goes to law school, gets a job at a firm.
sentences.zh: 于是他上了法学院，在一家律师事务所找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: So I was a rookie.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时是个菜鸟。

sentences.en: And he ends up taking on several big cases, landmark cases, actually, on the issues of diversity in corporate America.
sentences.zh: 他最终接手了几个大案子，实际上是关于美国企业界多元化问题的里程碑式案件。

sentences.en: I also was very tenacious about it and uncovered what became known as the tech.
sentences.zh: 我也对此非常执着，并揭露了后来被称为“科技”的东西。

sentences.en: Cyrus's first big case was in the 90s, when he took on Texco, the giant oil company, and he represented a number of Black employees who felt like they were reaching a ceiling in
sentences.zh: 赛勒斯的第一个大案是在90年代，当时他起诉了石油巨头德士古公司，他代表了一些黑人员工，他们觉得自己在企业阶梯上遇到了天花板，

sentences.en: the corporate ladder, that they couldn't get any further, they couldn't make any more money at their positions, and they said there was a double standard where white employees
sentences.zh: 他们无法再进一步，无法在自己的职位上赚更多的钱，他们说存在一种双重标准，白人员工

sentences.en: were getting promoted ahead of them.
sentences.zh: 在晋升方面排在他们前面。

sentences.en: And he wins, at the time, the largest racial discrimination case of its kind.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了当时同类案件中最大的种族歧视案。

sentences.en: So after the Texaco victory, I was still a lawyer in my 30s, so I decided to branch out on my own.
sentences.zh: 所以在德士古案获胜后，我当时还是个30多岁的律师，所以我决定单干。

sentences.en: I had...
sentences.zh: 我有……

sentences.en: He then decides, okay, this is something I want to do full-time, and he starts his own law firm that is going to take on racial discrimination cases.
sentences.zh: 他随后决定，好吧，这是我想全职做的事情，于是他创办了自己的律师事务所，专门处理种族歧视案件。

sentences.en: I had no clients, no staff, no office.
sentences.zh: 我没有客户，没有员工，没有办公室。

sentences.en: At the beginning, I just literally worked out of the trunk of a car with a couple of boxes.
sentences.zh: 起初，我真的只是在汽车后备箱里放着几个箱子办公。

sentences.en: And then, lo and behold, I get a call from one woman named Linda Ingram, who says, Cyrus, I have a case bigger than Texaco, and I'm at the Coca-Cola company.
sentences.zh: 然后，你猜怎么着，我接到了一个叫琳达·英格拉姆的女士的电话，她说，赛勒斯，我有一个比德士古案更大的案子，我在可口可乐公司。

sentences.en: So I remember vividly, I fly down to Atlanta, meet her at the car rental place.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得很清楚，我飞到亚特兰大，在租车处见到了她。

sentences.en: I followed her to this meeting at a law office in Atlanta, and the place was jam-packed.
sentences.zh: 我跟着她去亚特兰大一家律师事务所参加会议，那个地方挤满了人。

sentences.en: And I walked around the room, talked to everybody, and I heard a very similar story at Coke that I heard at Texaco.
sentences.zh: 我在房间里走来走去，和每个人交谈，我在可口可乐听到的故事和在德士古听到的非常相似。

sentences.en: The frustration of very impressive African-American executives, managers, who hit the glass ceiling.
sentences.zh: 那些令人印象深刻的非裔美国高管和经理们在遇到玻璃天花板时的挫败感。

sentences.en: And when I started the meeting, at one point, I said, tell me where stock options are, and
sentences.zh: 当我开始会议时，有一次我说，告诉我股票期权在哪里，

sentences.en: I'll tell you where the glass ceiling is.
sentences.zh: 我就能告诉你玻璃天花板在哪里。

sentences.en: Where that pay grade, where wealth is created, is where African-Americans are being locked out.
sentences.zh: 财富创造的薪酬等级所在之处，就是非裔美国人被拒之门外的地方。

sentences.en: So Cyrus takes this Coca-Cola case and ends up winning an even larger settlement, which is a record at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以赛勒斯接手了这个可口可乐案，并最终赢得了更大的和解金，这在当时是一个记录。

sentences.en: So he's been able to pull off two landmark settlements against these really powerful American corporations.
sentences.zh: 所以他成功地针对这些强大的美国公司达成了两项里程碑式的和解。

sentences.en: How's he doing it?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Well, what Cyrus did, particularly in the Coke case, was he used statistics to prove discrimination, stock options, promotions, salaries.
sentences.zh: 嗯，赛勒斯所做的是，特别是在可口可乐案中，他利用统计数据来证明歧视，包括股票期权、晋升、薪水。

sentences.en: And that was the crux of his cases.
sentences.zh: 这就是他案件的核心。

sentences.en: So Cyrus is using numbers, this hard data you're describing, to make it much harder for these companies to deny a behavior or a pattern of discrimination.
sentences.zh: 所以赛勒斯正在使用数字，也就是你描述的这些硬数据，让这些公司更难否认歧视行为或模式。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: How does all of this lead to the Rooney Rule?
sentences.zh: 这一切是如何引出鲁尼规则的？

sentences.en: Well, right around Martin Luther King Day in 2002, Cyrus wakes up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就在2002年马丁·路德·金纪念日左右，赛勒斯醒了过来。

sentences.en: And every day, like I always do, I started reading the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 每天，像往常一样，我开始读报纸。

sentences.en: Grabs the newspaper, does what he always does.
sentences.zh: 拿起报纸，做他一直做的事情。

sentences.en: He starts with the sports section.
sentences.zh: 他从体育版开始看。

sentences.en: And on that day was the announcement that Tony Dungy was fired by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
sentences.zh: 那天宣布的消息是托尼·邓吉被坦帕湾海盗队解雇了。

sentences.en: What I thought was shocking news.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得这是令人震惊的消息。

sentences.en: One of the first stories he reads is about Tony Dungy, a black coach with the Tampa Bay
sentences.zh: 他读到的第一批故事之一是关于托尼·邓吉的，一位黑人教练，他在坦帕湾

sentences.en: Buccaneers who was fired, even though he took one of the worst franchises in the NFL and turned it into a real success story.
sentences.zh: 海盗队被解雇了，尽管他把 NFL 最差的球队之一变成了一个真正的成功故事。

sentences.en: And I'm fuming, reading this paper.
sentences.zh: 我读着报纸，气得火冒三丈。

sentences.en: He started to think that maybe there was a racial discrimination pattern amongst the head coaching jobs.
sentences.zh: 他开始认为主教练职位之间可能存在种族歧视模式。

sentences.en: So I just had this epiphany that I could use statistics just like I did with Texaco and just like I did with Coca-Cola.
sentences.zh: 所以我突然意识到，我可以像在德士古和可口可乐那样使用统计数据。

sentences.en: And I had this hypothesis that if you ran the numbers, it would show that black head coaches went to the playoffs more often, won more games, and were last hired, first fired.
sentences.zh: 我有一个假设，如果你运行这些数字，它会显示黑人主教练进入季后赛的频率更高，赢得的比赛更多，而且是最后被聘用，最先被解雇。

sentences.en: And then I said, OK, let's see if we can test this.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，好吧，让我们看看能不能验证一下。

sentences.en: So Cyrus comes up with this plan to investigate what he thinks is racial discrimination in the
sentences.zh: 所以赛勒斯提出了这个计划，去调查他认为存在于 NFL 中的种族歧视。

sentences.en: NFL.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果你能改变美国的运动，你就能改变美国。

sentences.en: And I felt if you could change America's game, you could change America.
sentences.zh: 在美国，从招聘的角度来看，最引人注目的工作就是国家橄榄球联盟的主教练。

sentences.en: The most visible job in America in terms of hiring is the head coaches of the National
sentences.zh: 没人知道谁成了英特尔的新任首席执行官，或者也许人们会稍微关注一下埃隆·马斯克，但真的没人会盯着这些首席执行官看。

sentences.en: Football League.
sentences.zh: 这又回到了美国运动中发生的事情如何影响我们国家的心灵和思想。

sentences.en: No one knows who becomes the new CEO of Intel or maybe people follow Elon Musk a little bit, but like no one really watches the CEOs.
sentences.zh: 那么赛勒斯做了什么？

sentences.en: This comes back to what happens in America's game influences the hearts and minds of our country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，赛勒斯联系了另一位他一直在合作的律师。

sentences.en: So what does Cyrus do?
sentences.zh: 一起处理民权案件。

sentences.en: Well, Cyrus reaches out to another lawyer who he's been working on.
sentences.zh: 到那时，我已经每天都在和约翰尼·科克伦一起工作了。

sentences.en: Civil rights cases with.
sentences.zh: 一个叫约翰尼·科克伦的人。

sentences.en: By then, I'd been working with Johnny Cochran on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 等等，约翰尼·科克伦，那个辛普森案的律师？

sentences.en: A guy named Johnny Cochran.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是那个约翰尼·科克伦，他也是一位杰出的民权律师。

sentences.en: Wait, Johnny Cochran, the O.J.
sentences.zh: 所以赛勒斯去找约翰尼·科克伦说，我说，约翰尼，我有个主意。

sentences.en: Simpson guy.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你觉得针对 NFL 怎么样？

sentences.en: Yeah, that Johnny Cochran, who was also a prominent civil rights lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他的眼睛立刻亮了起来。

sentences.en: So Cyrus goes to Johnny Cochran and says, I said, Johnny, I have this idea.
sentences.zh: 他说，我全心全意支持。

sentences.en: Basically, what do you think about going after the NFL?
sentences.zh: 约翰尼也加入了这个想法。

sentences.en: And his eyes just lit up.
sentences.zh: 于是他们两人开始招募人员，开始计算 NFL 中黑人教练的数据，

sentences.en: And he was like, I'm all in.
sentences.zh: 胜负场次、他们在季后赛的表现等等，以及他们与白人教练的对比。

sentences.en: And Johnny gets on board with the idea.
sentences.zh: 当他们得到数据分析结果时，很明显他们有充分的理由。

sentences.en: So the two of them start out by recruiting someone to start crunching the numbers on black
sentences.zh: 黑人主教练，那少数有机会的人，进入季后赛的频率是白人主教练的两倍。

sentences.en: coaches in the NFL, how many wins and losses, how they do in the playoffs and so forth, and how they stack up against white coaches.
sentences.zh: 在16场比赛的赛季中，平均而言，他们每赛季赢球超过9场。

sentences.en: And when they got the results of the data analysis, it was pretty obvious they had a case to make.
sentences.zh: 白人教练每赛季赢球8场或更少。

sentences.en: Black head coaches, the handful that had the opportunity, went to the playoffs twice as often as white head coaches.
sentences.zh: 你可以从中看出，从未有过胜绩的白人教练会被聘用，然后被循环利用，再循环利用，而黑人主教练的表现则是季后赛，季后赛。

sentences.en: In a 16-game season, on average, they won more than nine games a season.
sentences.zh: 你可以直观地看到这一点。

sentences.en: White coaches won eight games or a little bit less per season.
sentences.zh: 你可以直观地看到这一点。

sentences.en: And you can just see in there that white coaches who never had a winning season would be hired
sentences.zh: 你可以直观地看到这一点。

sentences.en: and recycled and recycled and the black head coaches would be like, playoffs, playoffs.
sentences.zh: 你可以直观地看到这一点。

sentences.en: And you can just visually see.
sentences.zh: 你可以直观地看到这一点。

sentences.en: So they take the results, as well as stories from black coaches, and they write this big report that details discrimination in the NFL.
sentences.zh: 于是他们采纳了这些结果，以及黑人教练们的故事，写出了一份详述NFL歧视现象的长篇报告。

sentences.en: And they decide they need to release it publicly.
sentences.zh: 他们决定必须公开发布这份报告。

sentences.en: And so we came up with this idea of Monday Night Football, September 30th, 2002.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们想出了在2002年9月30日“周一橄榄球之夜”发布的主意。

sentences.en: And we said, let's just have a press conference right there before the game.
sentences.zh: 我们说，就在比赛前开个新闻发布会吧。

sentences.en: So they decide to hold a press conference before a Monday Night Football game in Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定在巴尔的摩的一场“周一橄榄球之夜”比赛前举行新闻发布会。

sentences.en: And they choose Shula's Steakhouse, a restaurant named for Don Shula, the legendary coach.
sentences.zh: 他们选择了舒拉牛排馆，这家餐厅是以传奇教练唐·舒拉的名字命名的。

sentences.en: We had 20 or so reporters.
sentences.zh: 当时大约有20名记者到场。

sentences.en: And we, one by one, went up and spoke.
sentences.zh: 我们一个接一个地上去发言。

sentences.en: The data person goes through the numbers.
sentences.zh: 负责数据的人员过了一遍数据。

sentences.en: And Cyrus speaks up about the case.
sentences.zh: 赛勒斯也针对这个案子发表了看法。

sentences.en: And then Johnny Cochran gets up.
sentences.zh: 然后约翰尼·科克伦站了起来。

sentences.en: And he says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: Literally, the first thing I remember Johnny saying is, if they don't negotiate, we're going to litigate.
sentences.zh: 我记得约翰尼说的第一句话就是：如果他们不谈判，我们就要诉讼。

sentences.en: If the NFL doesn't negotiate, they're going to litigate.
sentences.zh: 如果NFL不谈判，他们就要面临诉讼。

sentences.en: And that's what the reporters focused on.
sentences.zh: 而这正是记者们关注的焦点。

sentences.en: And with the threat of legal action out there, Cyrus sends copies of his report to the NFL.
sentences.zh: 在法律诉讼的威胁下，赛勒斯将他的报告副本寄给了NFL。

sentences.en: And unbeknownst to him, those reports are sent to every team owner.
sentences.zh: 他不知道的是，这些报告被送到了每一位球队老板手中。

sentences.en: And one of those owners was Dan Rooney.
sentences.zh: 其中一位老板就是丹·鲁尼。

sentences.en: Dan Rooney, as in the Rooney rule.
sentences.zh: 丹·鲁尼，也就是“鲁尼规则”里的那个鲁尼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Dan Rooney is this pivotal figure in NFL history.
sentences.zh: 丹·鲁尼是NFL历史上举足轻重的人物。

sentences.en: He's the son of Art Rooney, who bought the Steelers in the 1930s for $2,500.
sentences.zh: 他是阿特·鲁尼的儿子，阿特在20世纪30年代以2500美元买下了钢人队。

sentences.en: And Dan and his brothers grew up with the team.
sentences.zh: 丹和他的兄弟们是跟着球队一起长大的。

sentences.en: Dan was a water boy.
sentences.zh: 丹曾做过球童。

sentences.en: He hung out with the players back then.
sentences.zh: 那时他经常和球员们混在一起。

sentences.en: And he basically goes into the family business.
sentences.zh: 后来他基本上接手了家族生意。

sentences.en: But he isn't just focused on football.
sentences.zh: 但他不仅仅关注橄榄球。

sentences.en: Dan had kind of high ideals.
sentences.zh: 丹有着很高的理想。

sentences.en: And in the 60s, he hired the first black executive in league history who had been analyzing players who were playing in historically black colleges and universities.
sentences.zh: 60年代，他聘请了联盟历史上第一位黑人高管，此人之前一直负责分析历史悠久的黑人学院和大学里的球员。

sentences.en: And the Pittsburgh Steelers transformed into this powerhouse in the 70s, largely because of Dan's vision.
sentences.zh: 在70年代，匹兹堡钢人队转型成为一支劲旅，这很大程度上归功于丹的远见。

sentences.en: And Dan Rooney, sitting in his office in Pittsburgh, maybe with a copy of the report in his hand, writes a letter to Commissioner Tagliabue.
sentences.zh: 丹·鲁尼坐在匹兹堡的办公室里，手里可能拿着那份报告，给塔利亚布专员写了一封信。

sentences.en: So Dan Rooney reads this report, and he sends a letter to the NFL commissioner and tells him.
sentences.zh: 丹·鲁尼读了这份报告，他给NFL专员写了封信，告诉他：

sentences.en: It's not you, Paul, that needs to solve this.
sentences.zh: 保罗，解决这个问题的人不是你。

sentences.en: It's us, the owners, that have to take responsibility.
sentences.zh: 是我们，是老板们，必须承担起责任。

sentences.en: We have to hold each other accountable on this.
sentences.zh: 我们必须在这件事上互相监督。

sentences.en: The owners are the ones that need to take responsibility for this.
sentences.zh: 老板们才是需要为此负责的人。

sentences.en: The commissioner turns around and starts a diversity committee of other owners and puts Dan Rooney in charge.
sentences.zh: 专员转头成立了一个由其他老板组成的多元化委员会，并让丹·鲁尼负责。

sentences.en: The day Dan Rooney was announced as the chair of the diversity committee, and that hit the newspapers,
sentences.zh: 当丹·鲁尼被宣布为多元化委员会主席的消息见报那天，

sentences.en: John Wooten, former player and activist and at one point the highest ranking African-American club executive,
sentences.zh: 约翰·伍顿，前球员、活动家，也曾是级别最高的非裔美国人俱乐部高管，

sentences.en: he called me up and I was in the grocery store and I pick up the phone and, hey, Wootz, what's up?
sentences.zh: 他给我打来电话，当时我正在杂货店，我接起电话说，嘿，伍茨，怎么了？

sentences.en: He goes, we have just won.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们刚刚赢了。

sentences.en: And I said, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 我说，你什么意思？

sentences.en: He said, Dan Rooney is the chair of the diversity committee.
sentences.zh: 他说，丹·鲁尼是多元化委员会的主席。

sentences.en: He is the most influential owner and he has a track record of fairness.
sentences.zh: 他是最有影响力的老板，而且他一向以公正著称。

sentences.en: We have just won.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚赢了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在黑胶唱片时代做夜店DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个活生生的、快闪式的博物馆，里面摆满了精美的50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》APP？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: So Ken, what happens after Dan Rooney is named chair of this diversity committee for the NFL?
sentences.zh: 那么肯，丹·鲁尼被任命为NFL多元化委员会主席后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Dan Rooney hosted a meeting every week for eight weeks at NFL headquarters.
sentences.zh: 丹·鲁尼在NFL总部连续八周，每周主持一次会议。

sentences.en: Well, Dan Rooney sets out to convince the other owners, deliberately, slowly, but also urgently, because it's a matter of great importance to the league,
sentences.zh: 丹·鲁尼着手去说服其他老板，他深思熟虑、循序渐进，但也十分紧迫，因为这对联盟来说至关重要，

sentences.en: to adopt some of the recommendations that Cyrus Murray and Johnny Cochran made.
sentences.zh: 让他们采纳赛勒斯·默里和约翰尼·科克伦提出的一些建议。

sentences.en: They were afraid of Johnny.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕约翰尼。

sentences.en: They were afraid of me.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕我。

sentences.en: They kept us at a distance.
sentences.zh: 他们对我们敬而远之。

sentences.en: And what were those recommendations?
sentences.zh: 那些建议是什么？

sentences.en: Well, two of the three recommendations involved the use of draft picks.
sentences.zh: 三项建议中有两项涉及选秀权的使用。

sentences.en: So basically, they were designed to serve as incentives for teams to hire minority candidates.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它们旨在作为激励措施，鼓励球队聘用少数族裔候选人。

sentences.en: Those that did would get an extra draft pick.
sentences.zh: 聘用的球队将获得额外的选秀权。

sentences.en: And those that ran afoul of the rules would be penalized to draft pick.
sentences.zh: 而违反规则的球队将被扣除选秀权。

sentences.en: That part of the proposal went out the door like the first part of the conversation.
sentences.zh: 提案的那部分内容就像对话的第一部分一样，直接被否决了。

sentences.en: Those were rejected outright and quite vociferously because draft picks in the NFL are gold.
sentences.zh: 那些建议被断然且非常激烈地拒绝了，因为在NFL，选秀权就是黄金。

sentences.en: They're currency.
sentences.zh: 它们是硬通货。

sentences.en: They are the future of the franchise.
sentences.zh: 它们是球队的未来。

sentences.en: And having fewer of them puts you at a competitive disadvantage.
sentences.zh: 拥有的选秀权越少，你在竞争中就越处于劣势。

sentences.en: So two of the three recommendations, it sounds like, were non-starters.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来，三项建议中有两项是根本行不通的。

sentences.en: What about the third?
sentences.zh: 那第三项呢？

sentences.en: Well, the third recommendation was to obligate each team that had a head coach vacancy to interview at least one minority candidate.
sentences.zh: 第三项建议是要求每支有主教练空缺的球队必须面试至少一名少数族裔候选人。

sentences.en: The idea was to broaden their perspective and range of candidates and not simply interview white coaches over and over again.
sentences.zh: 其目的是拓宽他们的视野和候选人范围，而不是简单地一遍又一遍地面试白人教练。

sentences.en: I've always championed the idea of a diverse slate so you get as many people in in that final interview because you have to have at least a pipeline.
sentences.zh: 我一直支持多元化候选人名单的理念，这样你就能让尽可能多的人进入最终面试，因为你必须至少有一个人才储备库。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: You might discover somebody that might have been overlooked.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现某个原本被忽视的人才。

sentences.en: And it turns out that this third proposal was the most palatable to the owners.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这第三项提案是老板们最能接受的。

sentences.en: And at the end of 2002, Dan Rooney suggests that the owners adopt it.
sentences.zh: 2002年底，丹·鲁尼建议老板们采纳它。

sentences.en: And in December of 2002, they take a vote and they got a handshake to approve it.
sentences.zh: 2002年12月，他们进行了投票，并达成了口头协议。

sentences.en: And it becomes what is now known as the Rooney rule.
sentences.zh: 它就成了现在众所周知的“鲁尼规则”。

sentences.en: And the way I found out is Len Shapiro of the Washington Post called me up and he said, hey, Cyrus, what you've been advocating for has just succeeded.
sentences.zh: 我是从《华盛顿邮报》的莱恩·夏皮罗那里得知的，他打电话给我说，嘿，赛勒斯，你一直倡导的事情刚刚成功了。

sentences.en: Oh, by the way, should we call this the Cochran Mary rule or the Mary Cochran rule?
sentences.zh: 哦，顺便问一下，我们应该叫它“科克伦-默里规则”还是“默里-科克伦规则”？

sentences.en: And I said, no, let's call it the Rooney rule.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，叫它“鲁尼规则”吧。

sentences.en: Cyrus Mary decided that it would probably be best to use Dan Rooney's name because it would allow the league to take ownership over the issue as opposed to either a generic name or
sentences.zh: 赛勒斯·默里认为最好使用丹·鲁尼的名字，因为这会让联盟对这个问题产生主人翁意识，而不是使用一个通用的名字，

sentences.en: even Cyrus's name.
sentences.zh: 甚至也不是赛勒斯的名字。

sentences.en: Because I knew from my cases with Texaco and Co., the more you can make reforms organically from within, the more likely they'll succeed.
sentences.zh: 因为我从德士古公司等案子中了解到，改革越能从内部有机地产生，就越有可能成功。

sentences.en: And this meant the NFL has to take pride on its success.
sentences.zh: 这意味着NFL必须为自己的成功感到自豪。

sentences.en: And it would show that Dan Rooney was kind of the moral force and the moral compass of the league.
sentences.zh: 这也表明丹·鲁尼是联盟的道德力量和道德指南针。

sentences.en: Plus, Rooney rule sounds a lot better.
sentences.zh: 再说，“鲁尼规则”听起来好听多了。

sentences.en: And putting his name on it was kind of a nice piece of branding.
sentences.zh: 把他的名字冠在上面是一种很好的品牌推广。

sentences.en: And so when I was done with the reporter, I called up Johnny and we put out a statement
sentences.zh: 所以当我和记者谈完后，我给约翰尼打了电话，我们发表了一份声明，

sentences.en: that applauded the NFL for this giant step forward, but also raised warning signs about implementation and about enforcement.
sentences.zh: 对NFL迈出这一巨大进步表示赞赏，但也对执行和落实提出了警告。

sentences.en: Literally, that next weekend, we had to put the hammer on the NFL because Jerry Jones, the owner of the Dallas Cowboys.
sentences.zh: 就在那个周末，我们不得不向NFL施压，因为达拉斯牛仔队的老板杰里·琼斯……

sentences.en: So the Rooney rule got off to a rocky start.
sentences.zh: 所以“鲁尼规则”的开局并不顺利。

sentences.en: Jones trying to recruit Parcells.
sentences.zh: 琼斯试图招募帕塞尔斯。

sentences.en: The Dallas Cowboys owner, Jerry Jones, was trying to hire a white coach who was in demand.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯牛仔队老板杰里·琼斯试图聘请一位炙手可热的白人教练。

sentences.en: And he knew he had to interview at least one black coach, but he only gave one black coach
sentences.zh: 他知道他必须面试至少一名黑人教练，但他只给了那位黑人教练

sentences.en: a 20 minute interview on the phone, which was basically violating the spirit of the Rooney rule.
sentences.zh: 一次20分钟的电话面试，这基本上违背了“鲁尼规则”的精神。

sentences.en: And they suffered no consequences whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有受到任何惩罚。

sentences.en: And so Johnny and I put out a statement saying, that's not what we meant.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰尼和我发表了一份声明说，这并不是我们的本意。

sentences.en: And I'm calling up to the league's council.
sentences.zh: 我给联盟的法律顾问打了电话。

sentences.en: I'm saying, this isn't what we meant.
sentences.zh: 我说，这并不是我们的本意。

sentences.en: Shortly thereafter, the Detroit Lions president, Matt Millen, was found out to not have interviewed any minority candidates for their head coach vacancy.
sentences.zh: 此后不久，底特律雄狮队总裁马特·米伦被发现没有为他们的主教练空缺面试任何少数族裔候选人。

sentences.en: We then, that was a signature moment in the history of the rule.
sentences.zh: 那之后，成了该规则历史上的一个标志性时刻。

sentences.en: Because we said to them, this is make or break, them being the league.
sentences.zh: 因为我们对他们说，这是成败的关键，他们指的是联盟。

sentences.en: Either you enforce the rule, or you have no rule and it'll be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 要么你们执行规则，要么规则名存实亡，它会被摧毁。

sentences.zh: 他们考虑了一下，对马特·米伦处以20万美元罚款，因为他违反了规则。

sentences.en: And they said- He was fined $200,000.
sentences.zh: 他们说——他被罚款20万美元。

sentences.en: And the commissioner of the league said that the next time it happened, the executive would be fined at least $500,000.

sentences.en: That sent a resounding message to the NFL community.
sentences.zh: 这向NFL社区发出了一个响亮的信号。

sentences.en: So what followed was a remarkable run of success.
sentences.zh: 随后迎来了一段非凡的成功时期。

sentences.en: After this, the number of black coaches steadily started to increase from three to five to six to seven.
sentences.zh: 此后，黑人教练的数量开始稳步增加，从三个到五个，到六个，再到七个。

sentences.en: And in 2007, there's a major milestone.
sentences.zh: 2007年，出现了一个重要的里程碑。

sentences.zh: 洛维·史密斯，成为第一位站在超级碗赛场边线上的黑人教练。

sentences.en: That's a part of the story.
sentences.zh: 这是故事的一部分。

sentences.en: Tony Dungy, who became the second one on the other sideline.
sentences.zh: 托尼·邓吉，成为另一边赛场边线上的第二位。

sentences.en: Right now, I'm really focused on winning this game.
sentences.zh: 现在，我真的专注于赢得这场比赛。

sentences.en: On this historic day, where you and your friend Lovie Smith become the first African-American
sentences.zh: 在这个历史性的日子里，你和你的朋友洛维·史密斯成为第一批带领球队进入超级碗的非裔美国人

sentences.en: coaches to take teams to the Super Bowl, how much does that and this moment mean to you?
sentences.zh: 教练，这一刻对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: It means a lot.

sentences.zh: 我为能代表非裔美国人教练感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: Tremendous job they did.

sentences.en: I mean, you've been chipping away at this for years.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你多年来一直在为此努力。

sentences.zh: 你如何看待这种动态？

sentences.zh: 嗯，我感到一丝悲伤，因为我想，天哪，这完全回到了原点。

sentences.zh: 我与美国企业界的种族歧视斗争了近30年。

sentences.en: And I can tell you, it is a tenacious foe that are built in, in-group favoritism, the bias that people have in terms of selecting people, that they have preconceived notions.

sentences.en: Racial progress is fragile and you can lose it in a heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 种族进步是脆弱的，你可能在瞬间失去它。

sentences.en: And that's what I think the last 20 years showed.
sentences.zh: 我认为过去20年所展示的正是这一点。

sentences.en: We had great reform, great progress, leadership, people seizing opportunities, winning Super Bowls.
sentences.zh: 我们曾有过伟大的改革、巨大的进步、领导力，人们抓住机会，赢得了超级碗。

sentences.en: And then you take your foot off the gas, you make one mistake, and the house came tumbling down.
sentences.zh: 然后你松开了油门，犯了一个错误，一切就土崩瓦解了。

sentences.en: And that's what happened.
sentences.zh: 这就是发生的事情。

sentences.zh: 那么，肯，关于布莱恩·弗洛雷斯提起的诉讼，弗洛雷斯似乎是在说，为了增加多样性而制定的鲁尼规则，

sentences.en: really just isn't working.
sentences.zh: 实际上根本不起作用。

sentences.en: To turn it around.
sentences.zh: 扭转局面。

sentences.zh: 他们呼吁完全废除鲁尼规则。

sentences.zh: 这是因为他们认为该规则太无效了，应该被取消。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 赛勒斯对此有何看法？

sentences.en: No, you don't do that.
sentences.zh: 不，你不能那样做。

sentences.en: Senate and the Congress based on something I wrote.
